_comment: The three SELF-RESOLVING dialog methods from SRD §4.2's vocabulary table — select, confirm, input — arrive one after another mid-turn, each blocking the emission sequence until it is answered. This is ISC-111: a dialog request must be answered {cancelled:true} within ui_request_timeout, and the only way to time that honestly is for the double to actually withhold the turn, so `await_response: true` holds turn_end and agent_end behind all three. They are emitted SEQUENTIALLY rather than in a batch because that is what a real agent does — it asks, it waits, it asks again — and because a supervisor that answered only the first would otherwise never be caught. `self_resolve_ms` is set to 8000 on all three, which is §4.2's optional timeout modelled rather than a safety valve: it sits well clear of ui_request_timeout, so a supervisor answering anywhere inside its own bound always wins the race, and a run where NOTHING answers still finishes — with `unblocked_by: "self_resolve"` recorded against every dialog, which is the assertion that fails. Without it an unanswered run would burn the whole deadline_s and the test would die of its own budget instead of saying what went wrong. `editor` is deliberately absent: it has no timeout of its own and belongs to ISC-112, in ui-editor.json.
